A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIPO and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Inspection of all 23 v1 pages and 26 v2 pages supports reliable matching despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, personalization win rates, benchmark accuracy, diversity measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, negative-sampling experiments, and 70B-model results.

M1.justification: v2 broadens augmentation options through explicitly described response reshuffling and multiple negatives per positive (Section 4.2 and Table 6). These are limited procedural variants; the reference-policy MI objective and DPO loss remain unchanged. Matching retained benchmark scores does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: MMLU's knowledge-question-answering coverage is removed from Table 2 and Appendix C.1. Community Alignment, PRISM, Multifaceted Bench, GSM8k, SVAMP, and both ARC tasks remain. The 70B experiments reuse Multifaceted Bench rather than introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAMI as a distinct comparator throughout Table 1 and exact-answer, binary-reward RLVR throughout Table 2. v1's LLM-scored comparator called RLVR is retained under the name RLAIF; that rename is not itself a new baseline.

E3.justification: New settings include Llama-3.3-70B with rank-32 LoRA, pairwise evaluation by four proprietary judges, and response-order reversal to control position bias. v2 also introduces binary exact-match RLVR and negative-count sweeps. These substantially extend the experimental design without establishing changes to retained experiments' splits or budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds random-alphanumeric negative controls, sensitivity to 1/3/5/10 negatives, learning curves, and evaluation across different judges. Table 5 reworks the earlier joint prompt-context comparison into explicit reshuffling comparisons, extends sampling analyses to math/ARC, and drops the 7B sampling ablation. Existing diversity, critic, entropy, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain three-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting and the Qwen-7B exception in Appendix D. Although v2 shortens Table 1's caption, the full documents do not establish increased run counts or new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds SAMI, exact-match RLVR, negative-control, and 70B results, including 54.2–61.9% win rates in Figure 3, while removing MMLU scores. Existing values also change: Table 1's Llama-1B InfoNCE PRISM score changes from 80.93±1.86 to 84.88±1.49. Some revised MIPO entries correspond to different negative variants in Table 5, so they are not uniformly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds SAMI's symmetric mathematical objective and revises the marginal-sampling account: prompt-only personalization negatives are described as direct samples rather than approximations, while v1's explicit prompt-dependent eligible-context restriction is omitted. The central DPO/InfoNCE density-ratio derivation is retained; making reference-policy notation explicit largely clarifies existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains contrastive augmentation with DPO using reference-policy pointwise mutual information, without additional preference labels or verifiers. The headline personalization and general-task improvement claims remain. More precise instruction-following terminology and additional scale experiments primarily clarify or support those retained claims.

C2.justification: Unlike v1's largely summarizing Section 7, v2 explicitly discusses judge biases, GPT-4o-inferred contexts, the realism-versus-evaluation tradeoff, and dependence on initial capabilities and prompt diversity. It also adds substantive hypotheses about fixed-reference rewards, online MI reward hacking, reshuffling failures, and limited improvement on heavily trained benchmarks.

D1.justification: v2 replaces promised future code sharing with a concrete repository address and removes the earlier contrastive-data release promise. It newly supplies personalization train/test counts, 70B LoRA details, and self-revision and judge prompts. Appendix D's principal hyperparameters remain unchanged; newly disclosed sample counts do not establish resplitting.

R1.justification: The already-cited Fränken et al. work is explicitly positioned as the closest approach, with SAMI contrasted against MIPO's DPO integration and general-task applicability. v2 adds references including LoRA, Jaques et al. (2019), and Abdulhai et al. (2026), while removing MMLU and several classic intrinsic-MI references.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanations, and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting. v2 adds Section 4.2, reorganizes results into five findings, relocates InfoNCE formalism into the preliminaries, and substantially expands the limitations discussion. The title, terminology, publication information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds learning-curve Figure 2, 70B-comparison Figure 3, and negative-count Table 6. Tables 1 and 2 change comparator structure, Table 2 loses its MMLU column, and Table 5 becomes a wider cross-task comparison. The original schematic, diversity displays, and entropy plots are retained or relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through direct SAMI comparison, genuine exact-answer RLVR controls, negative-sampling controls, and 70B evaluation across four judges. Its explicit limitations and reproducibility disclosures substantially improve assessment of the central claims. These gains outweigh reduced MMLU coverage and reporting weaknesses, although numerical checking remains necessary: Table 2 reports Qwen-1.5B SFT's average as 71.33, whereas its four listed scores average 66.89.
